key_insight: COVID-19 vaccination was associated with better overall survival among cancer patients in Northwestern Russia, but the observational study does not establish causation.
clinical_relevance: AI-detected COVID-19 pneumonia on baseline chest CT was independently associated with poorer survival, alongside the study’s vaccination–survival findings.
method: Linked cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-analyzed chest CT data for 1,144 cancer patients.
Compared survival using Kaplan–Meier analysis and adjusted Cox regression.
Used March and November 2021 landmark analyses to reduce immortal time bias.
evidence_signal: In the primary landmark cohort (n=1,136), vaccinated patients had higher 3-year survival (80.3% vs. 45.7%) and lower adjusted all-cause mortality hazard (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25–0.64); the later landmark analysis showed an attenuated association (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.34–0.92).
watch_item: Only 76 patients received vaccination, and differences in cancer stage and active treatment leave potential residual confounding despite adjustment.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
